videos.title: Claude connectors explained: how Claude reaches your apps
videos.summary: Claude can't see inside your calendar or inbox until you connect them. A connector is a key to one app: you sign in yourself, Claude gets the same access your account has, and it asks before it sends, replies or forwards an email. Under the hood connectors run on MCP, an open standard Anthropic created. Every claim in the video comes from Anthropic's own help pages, linked below.

videos.title: Claude Code explained: it works inside your project
videos.summary: Not copy and paste. Claude Code reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands and tests, and checks its own work: gather context, take action, verify results. It runs in your terminal, VS Code, JetBrains, the desktop app, the browser and even Slack and GitHub. Permission modes decide what it can do without asking, and pressing Escape twice rewinds a change. Included with every paid Claude plan.

videos.title: How voice to text works: it hears numbers, not words
videos.summary: Drip asks how voice to text knows what he's saying. It doesn't get words: his one question arrives as 45,600 numbers (2.85 seconds at 16,000 a second), gets chopped into slices and stacked into a grid of how loud each note is, and a model guesses the words that most likely made it. Every number and grid in the video is measured from the video's own audio. Then the part newer AI dictation apps add: punctuation, and cutting the slip when you correct yourself.

videos.title: Same request, five websites: design skills for Claude
videos.summary: Drip asks Claude for a site for his coffee club and gets a familiar look: cream background, fancy serif, brown cup. So he gives the same request to five copies of Claude, one with no skill and one per design skill: Taste, Impeccable, UI UX Pro Max and Open Design. Every page in the video is a real build of the same brief. Impeccable's checker flagged 9 AI tells on the no-skill page and 0 on its own. Playwright then opened every page in a real browser at phone and laptop sizes: no sideways scroll on any of them.

videos.title: Jev vs ChatGPT: this AI doesn't write back
videos.summary: Ask a chatbot which of 200 customer emails are frustrated and it writes you a paragraph your code then has to turn back into yes or no. Jev, TypeSafe's new model, reads the same emails and hands back one answer per email with how sure it is, so your code can act on it. It's priced on what it reads, and it can't answer outside your options, though it can still pick the wrong one.
